Let's double-check fan tach diode direction with a typical 4-pin fan. Fan tach pin is open collector, needs pull-up. If pull-up is on MCU side of diode, when fan transistor on, it pulls cathode low, diode forward, MCU low. When fan transistor off, cathode floats; MCU pulled high through R2/R11, but diode anode high, cathode floating. If cathode floats, diode may not conduct, MCU high. If fan has internal pull-up to 12V, cathode 12, diode reverse, MCU high. OK. If fan has internal pull-up to 5V, cathode 5, diode reverse? Anode 3.3, cathode 5, reverse (cathode higher), MCU high. OK. Let's double-check fan tach diode direction with a typical 4-pin fan. Fan tach pin is open collector, needs pull-up. If pull-up is on MCU side of diode, when fan transistor on, it pulls cathode low, diode forward, MCU low. When fan transistor off, cathode floats; MCU pulled high through R2/R11, but diode anode high, cathode floating. If cathode floats, diode may not conduct, MCU high. However the fan side may have leakage or TVS to GND; if cathode floats, TVS pin1 A1 to cathode, pin2 GND. Bidirectional TVS doesn't pull. So cathode floats. MCU high. OK. If fan has internal pull-up to 12V, cathode 12, diode reverse, MCU high. OK. If fan has internal pull-up to 5V, cathode 5, diode reverse? Anode 3.3, cathode 5, reverse (cathode higher), MCU high. OK. If fan has internal pull-up to 3.3, cathode 3.3, anode 3.3, no drop, MCU high. OK. If fan low 0, anode 3.3, cathode 0, forward, MCU 0.7. OK. So direction correct.
